institution: Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences, Lucknow (Urology)
citation: SGPGIMS Hospital Infection Control Committee (SHICCOM). Hospital Infection Control Newsletter: Healthcare without infection, Volume 3, July to December 2021. Spotlight, Urology: antibiogram of the first 5 common bacterial pathogens in IPD and OPD samples (June to November 2021). Lucknow: SGPGIMS.
reporting: Percent susceptible for the five commonest bacterial pathogens from urine and pus samples (including PCN) of Urology IPD and OPD patients together, with the number of isolates per organism; "-" means not tested.
method: First isolate from any sample only; diagnostic isolates, not surveillance; drugs routinely tested; high level gentamicin and nitrofurantoin tested only in urine isolates. AST method and breakpoints not stated.

verification.note: Both tables on p 1 read from the PDF text layer (word positions per column) and compared value by value with the rendered page image (2026-09-26).

notes: Unit antibiogram of the Department of Urology, SGPGIMS Lucknow, June to November 2021, published in the SHICCOM Hospital Infection Control Newsletter (July to December 2021 edition). Positive cultures from urine and pus samples (including PCN, as printed; the page does not say whether PCN samples are counted as urine or pus) of IPD and OPD patients are pooled in each table: urine 967 and pus 53 of 1020 positive cultures (739 OPD, 281 IPD); mapped to urine (94.8% of positive cultures) and all locations. The first five organisms total 780 isolates (E. coli 409, E. faecalis 121, P. aeruginosa 115, K. pneumoniae 94, E. faecium 41), the same numbers as the table rows. The newsletter itself notes that an antibiogram should include species with at least 30 isolates tested.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: every cell of Tables 1 and 2 (p 1) re-read by eye from page renders (scale 5, the data rows again at scale 8) and written down before comparing with the file: all 54 cells and all 5 row n (121, 41, 409, 115, 94), with organism, specimen and setting. 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected. The "-" cells (not tested) are rightly left out.

Second reader: the validator's cells are printed that way: E. coli imipenem 34 and meropenem 61 (caution); tigecycline E. coli 100 and K. pneumoniae 88 (hidden for urine). K. pneumoniae amikacin 0 (next to gentamicin 45) was re-read at scale 8 and is printed 0.

Second reader: specimen mix as printed: Fig 1 counts 1020 positive cultures from "urine and pus samples (including PCN)" (OPD 739, IPD 281): urine 967 (94.8%) and pus 53 (5.2%). The page does not say whether PCN samples are counted as urine or pus, and gives no specimen split per organism; the tables cover the first 5 organisms (780 isolates, Fig 2). Spec urine and set all left as the extractor set them; the notes were reworded so that PCN is no longer placed under pus.

Lead 2026-09-26: a single-department antibiogram, given a focus ("Covers the urology department (urine and pus, including nephrostomy samples) only"): shown, never pooled with hospital-wide antibiograms, not a profile.
